one_line: Karkota kings of Kashmir who built a land‑grant based knowledge economy and expanded the valley’s power across North India.

appearance.age_look: Durlabhavardhana appears as a calm, broad‑shouldered man in his late 30s; Lalitaditya as a lean, intense warrior‑king in his early 30s, both athletic but dignified.
appearance.face: Durlabhavardhana has a rounded Kashmiri face, medium wheatish complexion, soft yet sharp brown eyes, neatly trimmed moustache, and a gentle, thoughtful default expression; Lalitaditya has a slightly longer face, similar complexion, keen dark brown eyes, a fuller moustache with short beard along the jawline, and a confident, focused default expression.
appearance.hair: Both have straight dark brown‑black hair; Durlabhavardhana’s is medium length, tied back in a low knot; Lalitaditya’s is slightly longer, pulled into a high warrior’s knot, and both wear a simple golden circlet crown with a small central leaf‑shaped ornament, Lalitaditya’s circlet subtly thicker.
appearance.costume: Durlabhavardhana wears a long‑sleeved white cotton tunic (angarkha style) reaching mid‑thigh with a wrapped overlap tied at the right, over fitted deep red trousers and soft brown leather boots; over this he has a light saffron‑orange woollen shawl draped from left shoulder across the chest and around the back, and a narrow dark green silk sash at the waist; simple gold stud earrings and a single thin gold necklace with a small round pendant complete his scholarly regal look. Lalitaditya wears a knee‑length light cream quilted tunic with faint checkered stitching, cinched with a wide dark maroon waist belt, over dull green fitted trousers and sturdier dark brown leather boots; over his shoulders rests a sleeveless bronze‑scale cuirass that covers chest and back but leaves the tunic visible at the edges, and a dark blue woollen cloak with a subtle border in muted gold drapes from his right shoulder and flows behind; he also wears small gold earrings and a thicker gold armlet on his right upper arm, keeping to practical but royal battlefield attire appropriate to 8th‑century Kashmir.
appearance.signature: Durlabhavardhana carries a rolled land‑grant palm‑leaf scroll tied with a red cord in his left hand, while Lalitaditya holds a long straight iron sword with a simple slightly curved cross‑guard and round pommel in his right hand, its plain scabbard hanging from his maroon belt.

ref_desc: Durlabhavardhana has a rounded wheatish face, low‑knot dark hair, white angarkha, saffron shawl, red trousers, scroll in hand, while Lalitaditya has a longer face, high‑knot hair, cream quilted tunic, bronze scale armour, blue cloak, sword, with white, saffron, red, blue, and bronze tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of two Kashmiri Karkota kings standing side by side: Durlabhavardhana as a broad‑shouldered, calm man with a rounded wheatish face, medium dark hair tied in a low knot, wearing a simple golden circlet, a long‑sleeved white angarkha‑style tunic overlapping to the right, fitted deep red trousers, soft brown boots, a saffron‑orange wool shawl draped from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back, a narrow dark green silk waist sash, small gold earrings and a thin gold necklace, holding a rolled palm‑leaf land‑grant scroll tied with a red cord. Next to him, Lalitaditya is lean and intense, with a slightly longer wheatish face, high‑knot dark hair, a thicker golden circlet, small gold earrings, a knee‑length light cream quilted tunic with faint checkered stitching, dull green fitted trousers, dark brown sturdy boots, a bronze scale cuirass over chest and back, a dark blue wool cloak with a muted gold border draped from his right shoulder and flowing behind, and a gold armlet on his right upper arm; his maroon belt supports a plain scabbard while he holds a long straight iron sword with a simple slightly curved cross‑guard and round pommel. Use a palette dominated by white, saffron orange, deep red, dark blue, and bronze, and show them clearly head‑to‑toe so every facial feature, hairstyle, garment layer, accessory, and their scroll and sword are easy to redraw consistently.
